claims.text: Selective laser melting can tune the magnetic behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Selective laser melting can tune the magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
SLM can generate enhanced dislocation densities in high-entropy alloys.
SLM can induce controlled nanometer-scale precipitates in non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
SLM-induced precipitates and dislocations alter magnetic exchange interactions.
Conventionally processed, slow-cooled non-equiatomic HEAs have a fairly uniform microstructure.
SLM processing can use controlled laser power and scan speed.
SLM laser power and scan speed can be selected to promote rapid solidification.
SLM processing of HEAs can be performed under an inert argon atmosphere.
Rapid solidification during SLM creates refined grain sizes and non-equilibrium precipitates.
Refined grains and non-equilibrium precipitates modify interatomic distances and local magnetic exchange interactions.
Changes in local magnetic exchange interactions influence magnetic entropy change and Curie temperature.
SLM-processed non-equiatomic HEAs will show a shifted magnetic transition temperature relative to conventionally processed counterparts.
SLM-processed non-equiatomic HEAs will exhibit an enhanced magnetocaloric effect, including increased magnetic entropy change.
Conventionally processed non-equiatomic HEAs have coarser microstructures and lower defect and precipitate concentrations than SLM-processed counterparts.
Magnetic-property tuning requires SLM parameters that produce significant microstructural modification.
